findings: BLOCKER: validate_recipe_data accepts recipes whose only write-capable node or sole final surface-binding node is inactive for the standard profile (for example minimum_profile=high-risk). A standard task can therefore bypass its write lane or terminal source binding and still derive succeeded. Require at least one standard-active writer and a standard-active final binder, and add negative recipe/profile regressions.

BLOCKER: live-claim staleness compares only the cooperative owner label. Releasing/reacquiring PROC-999 under the same label in a sibling worktree allowed show and begin to succeed without resume while state.branch/worktree remained bound to the old claim. Bind and compare the exact claim generation (for example claimed_at or a claim-record digest) plus owner/branch/worktree in show, transitions, and abort; add same-label same-worktree and sibling-worktree handoff regressions.

BLOCKER: the review surface is not frozen. Node surface_digest is populated only by finalize, so source edits after freeze_diff and after architecture/verification/docs review can be absorbed by finalize and the graph can report succeeded for an unreviewed final surface. Capture the post-write/freeze digest and reject downstream begin/finish/finalize when it changes until the write lane is reopened; add a source-change-after-review regression.

BLOCKER: show/list take no work-graph lock. A reader can observe the normal event-append to projection-replace window and fail with state/event projection mismatch; a deterministic delayed-write probe reproduced this while the writer completed normally. Serialize read snapshots under the graph lock or implement a bounded consistent-read retry, with a concurrency regression.

ROBUSTNESS: CLI task IDs are interpolated into Git-common-dir state/event paths without task_claim.TASK_ID_RE validation. Reject invalid IDs before resolving graph paths and add a traversal-shaped negative CLI test.
untested_surfaces: Automatic replay/repair after a real process crash between event append and projection replacement remains intentionally absent; schema v1 only detects the persistent mismatch.
No matched single-agent defect-recall, false-positive, human-time, latency, or model-cost baseline was run, so this review makes no efficiency claim.

findings: RESOLVED (was BLOCKER): validate_recipe_data now builds the standard-active node set and rejects a recipe whose final surface binder is not standard-active, or that has no standard-active write-capable node; run start repeats the check against the real task profile. Verified empirically: writer-pruned and binder-pruned copies of review-diamond.v1 both exit 2 with the matching diagnostics while the baseline validates. Negative regression: test_validator_rejects_profile_pruned_writer_and_final_binder.

RESOLVED (was BLOCKER): the claim binding is now a record digest over the whole claim record, which transitively covers a per-acquire uuid4 generation, compared alongside owner/branch/worktree on show, every transition, and abort. Verified that a same-second release/reacquire under an identical owner label yields identical claimed_at but a differing record digest. Regressions: test_same_label_reacquire_requires_explicit_resume and test_same_label_sibling_worktree_handoff_requires_resume, the latter over a real git worktree.

RESOLVED (was BLOCKER): the surface is frozen when the write lane finishes, stored as a run-level review binding, recomputed on every load, and enforced in the shared transition context, so any post-freeze edit hard-fails begin and finish rather than only finalize; the terminal binder additionally requires equality with the writer-frozen digest. Probes confirmed a mid-review edit, a new untracked file, and reopening a read-only node are all rejected, and only a write-lane reopen clears the binding. Regressions: test_review_surface_change_blocks_finalize_until_writer_reopens and test_terminal_surface_binding_becomes_stale_after_change.

RESOLVED (was BLOCKER): show and list acquire the same directory mutex the writers use before reading state and events, so the append-to-replace window is no longer observable; every _commit_event and every _load_state call site is inside the lock. Regression: test_show_and_list_wait_for_projection_lock holds the lock externally and asserts both readers block rather than read the window.

RESOLVED (was ROBUSTNESS): task IDs are validated in main() before the handler runs and again at all three Git-common-dir path-construction sites. Verified that all eight task-id-bearing subcommands reject a traversal-shaped id with exit 2 and create no state or event directory. Regression: test_cli_rejects_invalid_task_id_before_common_dir_path_resolution.

NEW, NON-BLOCKING: the lock stale-breaker compares a mkdir mtime that is never refreshed, so a writer holding the lock past 30 s can have it broken and its finally-rmdir then removes the successor lock; task_claim release/recover also skip the TASK_ID_RE check acquire applies. Accepted as out of scope for this task and routed to BUG-144; neither is reachable through a reviewed workflow today.
